questions.question: What problem does PagedAttention solve compared to a standard KV cache implementation?
options: It moves the KV cache from GPU to CPU to free up HBM for larger models
It manages KV cache as fixed-size blocks like virtual memory, keeping fragmentation under 4%
It compresses KV cache values using FP8 quantization to double effective capacity
It shares a single KV cache across all replicas in a multi-GPU cluster
questions.explanation: PagedAttention manages KV cache as fixed-size blocks in a block table — analogous to OS virtual memory. This eliminates the fragmentation and over-reservation that plagues contiguous-allocation schemes, keeping waste under 4% at production load.

questions.question: What is continuous batching in vLLM and what problem does it solve over static batching?
options: It batches all requests of the same prompt length together to avoid padding waste
It admits new requests and releases finished ones at every decode iteration without draining the batch
It continuously monitors GPU utilization and adjusts batch size accordingly
It splits long prompts into continuous chunks to prevent VRAM overflow
questions.explanation: Continuous batching works at the iteration level: when a sequence finishes decoding, it leaves the batch immediately and a waiting request takes its slot — without waiting for all sequences to finish. This eliminates head-of-line blocking from slow sequences.

questions.question: Chunked prefill in vLLM primarily protects which latency metric?
options: Mean throughput (tokens per second)
Mean TTFT across all requests
P99 TTFT tail latency
Mean TPOT (inter-token latency)
questions.explanation: Chunked prefill slices long prompts into smaller chunks and interleaves them with decode iterations. This prevents a single massive prefill from monopolizing the GPU and spiking decode latency for concurrent requests. It protects P99 TTFT, not mean throughput.

questions.question: A Llama 3.3 70B FP8 model on one H100 SXM5 with all three vLLM optimizations enabled at 128 concurrent requests achieves approximately how many tokens per second?
options: ~600 tok/s
questions.explanation: With PagedAttention, continuous batching, and chunked prefill all enabled, the lesson cites 2,200-2,400 tok/s — roughly 25% above vLLM's own default (~1,800) and 3-4x a naive PyTorch forward loop (~600 tok/s).

questions.question: What is the v0.18.0 compatibility gotcha teams hit when enabling every vLLM optimization at once?
options: PagedAttention and continuous batching conflict at >64 concurrent requests
Draft-model speculative decoding plus --enable-chunked-prefill does not compile; only N-gram GPU spec decode works in V1
FP8 quantization disables chunked prefill in V1 mode
KV cache offloading to CPU is incompatible with continuous batching
questions.explanation: vLLM v0.18.0 has a documented incompatibility: draft-model speculative decoding combined with --enable-chunked-prefill does not compile. The exception is N-gram GPU speculative decoding in V1, which is compatible with chunked prefill.

questions.question: What is the approximate P99 ITL (inter-token latency) improvement from adding chunked prefill under mixed prefill/decode load?
options: ~15 ms with chunked prefill vs ~50 ms without
~5 ms with chunked prefill vs ~10 ms without
~100 ms with chunked prefill vs ~200 ms without
No improvement — chunked prefill only reduces TTFT, not ITL
questions.explanation: The lesson's numbers show P99 ITL drops from ~50 ms (without chunked prefill) to ~15 ms (with it) under mixed load. Chunked prefill prevents long prefill batches from blocking decode iterations, directly improving the tail of inter-token latency.
